 Asean Club Championship Shopee Cup: Kuching City aims to continue to improve in competition 
 Photo: SPORTFIVE 
 BANGKOK: Asean Club Championship Shopee Cup title holders Buriram United FC will go into their Group A clash with Ho Chi Minh City Police FC under new management as Raúl Caneda makes his first appearance as head coach on Wednesday (Nov 18).
 The Spaniard was appointed two weeks ago to replace Mário Silva and will be leading the back-to-back champions into the region’s premier club competition for the first time when the Thai League 1 champions travel to Vietnam to take on Arthur Diles’ team.
 Both clubs picked up a point from the opening round of matches in Group A of the Asean Shopee Cup, with Caneda attempting to build on his positive start at the helm of the team.
 The former Al-Ittihad Club boss was in charge as Buriram United notched up a 0-0 draw against Kashima Antlers in the AFC Champions League Elite last week in a positive opening to the 57-year-old’s reign.
 “Everyone did a great job; I have nothing to encourage the players (to do) because they did their best and made a very big effort,” Caneda said after his side impressed in the meeting with the J1 League champions.
 Both Buriram United and Ho Chi Minh City Police drew against Borneo FC Samarinda and Ratchaburi FC respectively, while Malaysia’s Kuching City FC and Tampines Rovers FC from Singapore also drew their opener.
 Manila Digger FC will kick off their Group A campaign against Borneo on Wednesday after the play-off winners had a bye in the opening round, while Tampines Rovers will host Ratchaburi. Kuching City have the week off.
 Play in Group B on Thursday will be headlined by a heavyweight clash between 2024/25 tournament runners-up Công An Hanoi FC and Malaysia Super League champions Johor Darul Ta’zim FC in Hanoi’s Hàng Đẫy Stadium.
 JDT launched their challenge for the 2026/27 Shopee CupTM with a clinical 6-0 win over PKR Svay Rieng FC on Matchday 1, while Mano Pölking’s V.League 1 champions registered a 1-0 victory over hosts Lion City Sailors FC through Léo Artur’s goal in first-half stoppage time.
 Since that win, Công An Hanoi have gone to secure their first-ever victory in the AFC Champions League Elite with a 3-2 defeat of Chinese Super League side Shanghai Port FC to further boost the confidence of the Vietnamese champions.
 “I’m very proud to be part of this historic moment,” Pölking said after that win. “We still have a lot to learn from Shanghai Port, especially in terms of professionalism and organisation. We’re taking small steps, but the whole team can be proud.”
 Indonesia’s Persib Bandung won 3-1 in their Shopee CupTM opener against Port FC from Thailand and continue their quest for a place in the quarter-finals in their debut appearance in the competition when they host Myanmar’s Shan United FC.
 Shan United will be featuring in the competition for the first time this season after securing their place via the play-offs.
 PKR Svay Rieng, meanwhile, will look to bounce back from their heavy loss to JDT when they host Port in Phnom Penh with both clubs looking for their first points of the Shopee Cup 2026/27 season.
 FIXTURES 
 Wednesday, November 18 / Group A  
 Tampines Rovers FC (SGP) v Ratchaburi FC (THA), Jalan Besar Stadium, Singapore, 7.30pm (local) / 11.30am (GMT)
 Ho Chi Minh City Police FC (VIE) v Buriram United FC (THA), Bình Dương Stadium, Hồ Chí Minh City, 6pm (local) / 11am (GMT)
 Borneo FC Samarinda (IDN) v Manila Digger FC (PHI), Segiri Stadium, Samarinda, 8pm (local) / 12pm (GMT)
 Thursday, November 19 / Group B 
 Công An Hanoi FC (VIE) v Johor Darul Ta’zim FC (MAS), Hang Day Stadium, Hanoi, 7.30pm (local) / 12.30pm (GMT)
 PKR Svay Rieng FC (CAM) v Port FC (THA), Morodok Techo National Stadium, Phnom Penh, 7pm (local) / 12pm (GMT)
 Persib Bandung (IDN) v Shan United FC (MYA), Gelora Bandung Lautan Api Stadium, Bandung, 7pm (local) / 12pm (GMT)
